get.description: What applies to this assistant: the org's budgets and its own.

A short-lived link to the original file, for citation deep links.

Tenant scoping is the important part: ``svc.get`` filters by
``ctx.assistant.id``, and ``AssistantCtx`` has already 404'd if the caller
isn't a member of the assistant's org — so there's no path from "I know a
data source id" to "I can mint a URL for another tenant's object".

post.description:
Stop the turn running in this conversation (task 1.6).

202, because the stop is a request: the turn ends on its own stream, which
then closes with a normal `done`. It is published as well as tried
locally, since the turn may be streaming from a different worker.
Stopping a turn is changing the conversation, so the same rule applies as
for posting into it: its creator, or an admin.

The canvas's wiring rules, served from the same constants the validator

The alternative was a copy of the edge allow-list in TypeScript, which
would disagree with the backend the first time either side changed — and
the failure mode is silent (the canvas lets you draw an edge the API then
rejects, or refuses one it would have accepted). One source of truth
instead.

get.description: Liveness: the process is up. No dependency checks.

Readiness: database, Redis, object storage and (when the real driver
would run) the Claude CLI, checked concurrently, each within
`CHECK_TIMEOUT_S`. It used to check the database only.

503 when a critical check fails; 200 "degraded" when only a non-critical
one does; 200 "ok" otherwise. Each check's result is in `checks`.
